diagnosis: All 17 programs return the record to within $10^{-12}$, so the kicks, annealing, and LP polish are repeatedly falling back into the same basin. The plot shows roughly 820 essentially exact contacts—about six per point, versus only three tangent degrees of freedom per point on $S^3$—followed by a large slack gap to the next pairs. Only three points are rattlers with no contacts, while the remaining 269 form an over-rigid jammed core that alone determines the maximum. The missing structural property is therefore not local smoothness but a more balanced, collectively rearrangeable contact topology: one where load/contacts are shared more uniformly, no points are spectators, and a coordinated motion can exchange contacts instead of every perturbation being blocked and snapped back by the LP.

Repeated perturbation, annealing, and LP from the record or Hurwitz constructions therefore keep returning to essentially the same contact topology.

This is nearly isostatic: 272 points on $S^3$ have $272\cdot3-6=810$ nontrivial degrees of freedom, comparable to the $\sim$800 contacts, yet one point is a rattler and contact degrees are heterogeneous at about 4–10 instead of balanced. The projected contact graph looks amorphous, with no evident antipodal pairing, group-orbit regularity, Hopf/torus layering, or other global structure that would permit a coordinated improvement. Consequently LP polishing and ordinary annealing merely squeeze the inherited record basin—hence the total gain of only $3.5\times10^{-7}$—while random kicks either violate locked contacts or relax back to the same topology.

diagnosis: The left panel shows roughly 800 pairs tied within about $10^{-12}$ of the maximum, followed by a clear gap to $\sim10^{-5}$, so the active contact set is sharply defined and ordinary LP polishing inside this basin is exhausted. That count is close to the isostatic count $272\cdot3-6=810$, but contacts per point range from 0 to 10 around a mean of only $\sim5.9$, with one rattler and many 4-contact points coexisting with 9–10-contact hubs. The configuration therefore lacks a balanced, approximately 6-regular, positive-stress isostatic contact graph in which every point is comparably constrained, and the projection shows no compensating symmetry or antipodal regularity. Repeated convergence to exactly $0.8981599619373$ indicates that successful workers keep rediscovering the same basin, while perturbations either leave its contact topology unchanged or are too unstructured to find a better one.
